column1: # layout-map.tsv (harbor#1272, #949 standard points 2 and 5) - what every tracked top-level entry of harbor IS.
# WHY A NEW FILE. layers.tsv answers one question (core or dev: does it ship) and its rule is one row per path;
# kinds.tsv answers another (one row per KIND of artifact, with its fields). Neither has a row per ROOT ENTRY with
# both a kind and a layer, so folding it into either would bend that register. This file holds only what they do not:
# the entry, its kind, its #949 layer and a note. Whether an entry ships is NEVER stored here: it is read from
# layers.tsv (docs/context-map.md shows it). bin/lint-layout-map.sh is red on a tracked top-level entry with no row,
# on a row naming an entry that is not tracked, and on a kind or layer the registers do not have.
# Columns, tab-separated, one header row:  entry  kind  layer  note
#   entry  a top-level folder ending in "/", or a root file; exactly one row each
#   kind   a kinds.tsv id where one fits, else one of the words in the `# unregistered-kinds:` line below
#   layer  source | generated | record | report | deployed (terms.tsv, class layer); a mixed folder takes its majority and says so
#   note   one line: what it holds
# unregistered-kinds: config deploy-unit vendored command code
# A one-off dated document at the root is a `record`; moving it to a records folder is a later step of harbor#1272.
